candidates.title: Accelerated Transformation of Nitrite to Nitro-organic Compounds in Frozen Water in the Presence of Natural Organic Matter
candidates.authors: Yang, Peizeng; Chen, Jie; Ruan, Jingqi; Wu, Kai; Lu, Junhe; Kong, Deyang
candidates._abstract: Abstract Nitrite (NO2–) is a key intermediate in nitrogen cycling, yet its abiotic fate in frozen environments remains insufficiently understood, particularly its conversion to organic nitrogen. Here, we demonstrate that freezing dramatically accelerates NO2– oxidation and promotes its incorporation into natural organic matter (NOM), forming hazardous nitroaromatic compounds. At −20 °C and pH 4.0, nitrite removal exceeded 85% within 24 h, compared to negligible loss in liquid water. Confocal Raman and fluorescence imaging revealed strong enrichment of NO2– and NOM within quasi-liquid grain boundaries, accompanied by a localized pH drop from 4.0 to ∼1.2. These microenvironments favor the formation of reactive nitrogen species (HNO2 and NO+), which nitrate electro-rich moieties in NOM and initiate oxidative coupling reactions. Fourier transform ion cyclotron resonance mass spectrometry (FT-ICR-MS) identified a marked increase in nitrogen-containing formulas (from 1290 to 1440) and higher average molecular weight (Mn) of NOM (from 369.191 to 382.594 Da). Phenol served as a model substrate, confirming nitration and oligomerization pathways. These findings demonstrate that freeze-concentration effect induced acidification and nitrite speciation change act as significant drivers for the molecular-level transformation of NOM in ice, providing new insights into nitrogen geochemical cycling, nitroaromatic pollutants formation, and ecological risk in cryosphere and seasonally frozen waters under climate change.

candidates.title: Potential loss of salmonid spawning habitat in the Arctic due to rusting rivers
candidates.authors: Carey, Michael P.; Baughman, Carson A.; Koch, Joshua C.; Poulin, Brett A.; Hill, Kenneth R.; Scanlon, Brendan P. …
candidates.venue: Canadian Journal of Fisheries and Aquatic Sciences
candidates._abstract: Permafrost thaw is a disturbance impacting high-altitude and high-latitude environments. In northern Alaska, permafrost thaw is driving the mobilization of metals from soils and degrading the water quality of Arctic rivers. Due to the weathering of sulfide mineral deposits, river reaches can appear orange due to iron oxides either suspended in the water or deposited on the substrate creating the appearance of rusting rivers. A primary concern about rusting rivers is the negative effect on spawning habitat due to increasing metal concentrations above toxicity thresholds in surface waters or altering hyporheic flow. We examined the spatial overlap between spawning habitat of Dolly Varden ( Salvelinus malma) and rusting river degradation in northwest Alaska using a time-series of satellite imagery. Annual overlap between total Dolly Varden spawning area and degraded habitat ranged from 0% to 21% from 1986 to 2024. Spatial overlap of degraded water and spawning habitat varied temporally amongst watersheds. Spatial and temporal variability in the overlap of degraded water and spawning habitat indicates a complex interaction between rusting rivers, fish, and aquatic food webs.

candidates.title: Association of thermally-labile organic carbon with iron-bearing minerals in deep sediments of a small, Arctic clearwater lake
candidates.authors: Hazuková, Václava; Oderstad, Hanna; Olid, Carolina; Karlsson, Jan; Gudasz, Cristian; Boily, Jean‐François
candidates._abstract: The stabilization and persistence of organic carbon (OC) in soils and sediments is thought to be governed in large part by association with mineral matrices, especially reactive iron (Fe) phases. However, the role of these organo-mineral interactions has not been fully evaluated in lake sediments that are typically more OC rich. Here, we conducted detailed analyses of three sediment cores collected along a lake-depth gradient from a small clearwater lake in the Swedish Arctic to explore variability in sediment geochemistry and the role of mineral protection in OC preservation. While mineralogy of the two shallower, littoral cores was similar, mostly consisting of (alumino)silicates, sediments in the deepest part also included Fe-oxides and had 6–7 times higher specific surface area, indicating a greater potential for organo-mineral interactions. Higher specific surface area was strongly associated with more thermally-labile OC (ρ = −0.71, p = 0.01), but not with OC stocks (ρ = 0.05, p = 0.89). Multiple independent proxies indicated that deep-basin OC was more aliphatic, less degraded, and likely of planktonic algal origin compared to shallower regions. We suggest that the spatial pattern in OC quality is not simply a function of different OC sources or hydrodynamic sorting, but it is also regulated by differential capacity for organo-mineral stabilization.

candidates.title: Water and Sanitation in Rural Alaska: A Scoping Review
candidates.authors: Thelemaque, Nathalie A.; Kumpel, Emily; Butler, Caitlyn; Weston, Bessie; Williar, Charissa; Fuente, David E.
candidates._abstract: Abstract Communities in rural Alaska face persistent challenges in accessing safe, reliable, and affordable water and sanitation services because of extreme environmental conditions, geographic isolation, and economic vulnerabilities. Recent federal investment in infrastructure provides a timely opportunity to assess the state of the literature on water and sanitation in this region. This scoping review synthesizes findings from 114 studies on water and sanitation service delivery in rural Alaska across four thematic areas: water, sanitation, and health; household preferences and source choice; planning, governance, and finance; and engineered systems and climate change. The literature consistently links in-home piped water services to improved health outcomes. Research on household preferences highlights the influence of service reliability, taste, tradition, and cost on water use behaviors. Studies addressing planning, governance, and finance document fragmentation across institutional levels and high capital and operational costs. Research on engineered systems and climate change demonstrates that permafrost thaw and coastal erosion threaten infrastructure integrity and source water quality. Overall, the literature is generally descriptive and technical in nature, focusing primarily on public health and engineering systems. Gaps remain in our understanding of household preferences for service attributes, household coping costs, climate resilience, and service affordability.

candidates.title: A systematic review of the methods and magnitudes of dissolved oxygen exchanges in streams and rivers
candidates.authors: Krause, Jasmine; Knutson, Cassandra; Hotchkiss, Erin R.; Cohen, Matthew J.; Ward, Adam Scott
candidates._abstract: Dissolved oxygen (DO) has been extensively studied in streams and rivers, and its diel dynamics have become the primary lens through which whole-stream metabolism—gross primary production (GPP) and ecosystem respiration (ER)—is inferred. Yet this integrated signal emerges from the interaction of oxygen exchanges across stream compartments, and how these exchanges contribute to whole-stream signals remains less understood. To characterize the extent and nature of this disconnect, we synthesize 230 empirical studies (1964–2024) documenting which oxygen exchanges have been measured, by what methods, and at what magnitudes across streams and rivers globally. Here, we define oxygen exchanges broadly as all quantified transfers of oxygen into or out of stream compartments, organizing them into whole-stream metabolism (GPP and ER) as an integrative signal of four underlying process domains: (1) water column, (2) benthic, (3) hyporheic zone and sediments, and (4) surface-atmosphere exchange. Across these groupings, whole-stream metabolism and surface-atmosphere exchange dominated the literature, accounting for 66 and 18% of reported measurements, respectively, while individual process domains were far less common (benthic ~7%; sediment oxygen demand ~5%; water column ~4%; hyporheic ~1%). Subsurface respiration was the most variable yet least frequently measured exchange, and in the small subset of studies with concurrent process domains and whole-stream measurements, dominant respiration pathways shifted from subsurface-dominated in small streams to water column-dominated in large rivers. While these concurrent studies offer rare mechanistic insight, they represent a small subset of the literature, and the methodological and disciplinary fragmentation documented across our synthesis limits our ability to attribute whole-stream oxygen signals to their underlying processes. We identify key challenges including methodological heterogeneity and scaling barriers across compartments, inconsistent terminology and disciplinary silos that hinder integration of subsurface exchanges. Addressing these gaps through concurrent multi-compartment measurements, standardized reporting, and cross-disciplinary integration is essential to advancing a mechanistic understanding of stream oxygen dynamics.

candidates.title: Metals and PFAS concentrations in aquatic environments and fish of the Brooks Range, Alaska
candidates.authors: Fraley, Kevin M.; Snodgrass, Wyatt; Kelly, Benjamin T.; Robards, Martin D.
candidates._abstract: In Alaska, fish are an important subsistence resource for Indigenous and rural residents. Additionally, they can serve as bioindicators that respond to ecosystem changes. Resource development, such as mining, and climate change-impacted natural phenomena like permafrost thaw can introduce contaminants into aquatic systems. Consequently, quantification of contaminant concentrations in aquatic media is needed to track ecosystem and fish health in order to characterize current conditions and identify potential threats. To address gaps in fish contaminant data in northern Alaska, we assessed metals and per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) concentrations in waterbodies along the Dalton Highway associated with a 2026 land use change, and in three rivers of the western Brooks Range potentially affected by the proposed Ambler Road. Metal concentrations in aquatic media were not substantially elevated at most sites. In fish muscle tissue, mercury levels were largely below thresholds for consumption advice except for a subset of large-bodied individuals. PFAS were either not detected, or at trace concentrations (< 3 µg/kg) in most fish. However, perfluorooctanesulfonic acid (PFOS) was elevated in fish at one lake along the Dalton Highway near industrial infrastructure, with maximum observed concentrations reaching thresholds that would trigger further investigation or consumption advisories in at least 45 other US states and countries. Given the possible health implications for people and fish from PFAS exposure, we recommend further investigation of this site and similar industrial infrastructure outposts throughout Alaska, as well as call for PFAS fish consumption guidance to be formalized at the Alaska and US federal level.

candidates.title: Subglacial geology and thermal conditions regulate methane emissions from Svalbard glaciers
candidates.authors: Kleber, Gabrielle Emma; Mannerfelt, Erik Schytt; Schlömer, Stefan; Senger, Kim; Magerl, Leonard; Hensgens, Geert …
candidates._abstract: Melt rivers from valley glaciers and ice sheets release methane by transporting microbial or geologic methane from beneath glaciers, making it available for atmospheric emission. However, the mechanisms and magnitude of such methane release remain poorly understood due to limited studies. Here, we show how subglacial geology and glacier thermal conditions control methane supersaturation in meltwaters from 19 valley glaciers across central Svalbard. We find that all sampled meltwaters are supersaturated with methane, with peak concentrations up to 425-times atmospheric equilibrium. The carbon isotopic compositions of the methane and the presence of ethane and propane indicate that the methane is largely of thermogenic origin. Ground-penetrating radar surveys show that the extent of temperate ice at the glacier bed plays a critical role in facilitating methane acquisition, particularly in regions underlain by organic-rich, shale-dominated geological formations. This mechanistic insight is relevant for glaciated regions worldwide with organic-rich geology and suggests that accelerated glacier melt may amplify methane mobilization from beneath glaciers.

candidates.title: Potentially Toxic Elements in Spring Water of the Northern Ladoga Region: Speciation, Migration Intensity, and Sources
candidates.authors: Сидкина, Е. С.; Aidarkozhina, A. S.; Конышев, А. А.
candidates._abstract: The abundant water resources of the Northern Ladoga region are subject to anthropogenic pressures and geogenic influences associated with the distinctive geochemistry of the bedrock. Spring water is widely used for domestic purposes, including drinking. These waters are characterized by low salinity with a dominant Ca–HCO3 facies often enriched in SO42−. Geochemical signatures reflect sulfide and fluorite mineralization, particularly in springs near Pitkäranta, and are associated with elevated concentrations of Zn, Mn, Rb, Y, Cd, Mo, U, and Cu. NICA-Donnan speciation modeling indicates extensive complexation by dissolved organic matter (DOM) of Fe, Ni, Cd, Cu, Pb, U, Th, Co, and Al, with particularly stable complexes of Cu, Pb, U, and Th. Positive matrix factorization (PMF) modeling indicated that mining and its associated industrial heritage are the primary sources of potentially toxic elements, followed, to a lesser extent, by transport and road infrastructure, as well as natural sources.

candidates.title: Spatial evolution and geochemical controls of U- and Th-series radionuclides in acid mine drainage affected waters of the Odiel Basin, SW Spain
candidates.authors: Le, V.H.; Guerrero, José Luis; Bolívar, Juan Pedro; Guillén, Javier
candidates._abstract: Acid mine drainage (AMD) affects the mobility of naturally occurring radioactive materials (NORM), but its influence on the distribution of U- and Th-series radionuclides in polymetallic mining districts and downstream estuaries remains poorly understood. Here, we characterize the spatial evolution and isotopic signatures of U- and Th-series radionuclides in the dissolved fraction along the Oraque–Meca–Odiel river–estuary system (SW Spain). This system shows a strong geochemical gradient, from highly acidic AMD headwaters (locally pH < 3; high sulfate and metal concentrations) through weakly acidic reaches (pH ≈ 4.5) to near-neutral estuarine waters (pH ≈ 7). 238 U and 232 Th activity concentrations were strongly enriched in AMD-impacted headwaters, reaching values in the order of 10 3 and 10 2 mBq L −1 , respectively, with 238 U exceeding global riverine background by more than two orders of magnitude. PHREEQC modeling indicated that modeled aqueous U(VI) was dominated by free uranyl and uranyl-sulfate species under strongly acidic conditions. In contrast, dissolved 232 Th decreased more strongly than U as pH increased, producing a clear U Th geochemical decoupling. This pattern is consistent with the generally higher particle reactivity of Th reported in previous studies and suggests transfer from the dissolved phase during downstream evolution. 234 U/ 238 U ratios were generally >1, indicating isotopic disequilibrium and preferential 234 U mobilization. The 230 Th/ 232 Th activity ratios remained close to unity, indicating limited isotopic fractionation within the dissolved Th pool. These results show that the spatial variations of dissolved U and Th across the investigated river-estuary system coincided with hydrochemical gradients and changing source contributions, while the selected confluences showed nominal element-specific departures from the adopted sulfate-based mixing predictions.

candidates.title: Seasonal assessment of hydrochemical characteristics of rivers in the Bor mining area
candidates.authors: Adamović, Dragana; Nemeş, Nicoleta Sorina; Vasiljević, Sanela; Radović, Bojan; Urošević, Tamara; Đorđievski, Stefan …
candidates.venue: International October Conference on Mining and Metallurgy (IOC)
candidates._abstract: This study evaluates the current hydrochemical status of rivers in the Bor mining area through seasonal monitoring conducted from summer 2025 to spring 2026. Twelve sampling sites were analyzed for pH, electrical conductivity (EC), and sulfate concentrations. Background waters were characterized by the Ca-Mg-HCO₃ hydrochemical facies, whereas mining-affected rivers were dominated by the Ca-Mg-SO₄ facies. Elevated EC and sulfate concentrations downstream of the mining area confirmed the persistent influence of mining activities. Comparison with historical data revealed substantial improvement in water quality following mine wastewater treatment, although sulfate remains a reliable indicator of residual contamination.

candidates.title: Temperature dynamics in crevasse-drainage systems of Antarctic glaciers
candidates.authors: Parov, Tsvetan
candidates.venue: Journal of the Bulgarian Geographical Society
candidates.found_via: query “acid rock drainage glacier” ; query “acid rock drainage rock glacier”
candidates._abstract: During the 33rd Bulgarian Antarctic Expedition, field studies were conducted to examine the internal microclimate of crevasse-drainage systems of the three glaciers: Balkan Ice Field, Johnsons and Contell Glaciers. The research is focusing on the relationship between fluctuations of surface meteorology parameters, internal air glacier temperatures in the crevasses and possible connection with solar activity. The total duration of the study exceeds 60 days, making it the longest temperature monitoring of glacier crevasses in Antarctica. Measurements of air temperature, humidity, and atmospheric pressure were carried out using autonomous sensors, while ultrasonic anemometers recorded airflow direction and speed inside the crevasses. Sensors were placed at depths of up to 25 m in central zones and 10 m near the glacier edges. The study identified a distinct temperature gradient at 3-meter intervals and mapped the depth of zones with persistently negative temperatures. Increased solar activity was associated with lower internal glacier temperatures and stronger air circulation. A negative correlation was found between solar activity and both temperature and downward airflow within crevasses. A glacial cave under the Balkan Ice Field allowed access to subglacial waters and sediment sampling. For the period of one year, the ablation zone of the Balkan Ice Field had expanded, and the constant negative temperature zone had deepened by 6–7 m since the previous expedition. Contell Glacier showed greater thermal stability and resistance to change compared to the larger ice fields. The extended daylight in January (approximately 20 hours) facilitated reliable correlation with solar activity patterns.

candidates.title: ICEland-1: a geochronological database for reconstructing Late Quaternary glacier, relative sea level, and paleoclimate patterns in Iceland
candidates.authors: Harning, David J.; Geirsdóttir, Áslaug; Andrews, John T.; Barth, Aaron M.; Jónsdóttir, Ingibjörg S.
candidates.found_via: query “acid rock drainage glacier” ; query “acid rock drainage rock glacier”
candidates._abstract: Abstract. We present a comprehensive and quality-controlled chronological database for past glacier, relative sea level, and paleoclimate changes in Iceland during the Late Quaternary: ICEland-1. The database includes 1744 data points and metadata from 442 sites located in the marine and terrestrial realm, with dates derived from radiocarbon (14C), tephrochronology, and terrestrial cosmogenic nuclides (TCN). This filtering approach reveals significant spatiotemporal gaps in our understanding of Late Quaternary ice sheet, relative sea level, and paleoclimate variability in and around Iceland. We highlight several key avenues for future research that can help minimize existing spatiotemporal uncertainties and biases in the empirical data. The implementation of ICEland-1 for local ice sheet model calibrations and data-model comparisons will improve our understanding of past and future changes of ice sheets in the North Atlantic and Antarctica. candidates._abstract: This study examines the impact of geological, marine and anthropogenic sources on metal and metalloid concentrations in the forefields of four glaciers (Ecology, Sphinx, Tower and Windy) on King George Island, Antarctic. candidates.title: A non-destructive testing technique for localized electrical resistivity in heterogeneous rock

candidates._abstract: Accurately and non-destructively measuring the local resistivity of heterogeneous core samples is crucial for studying the mechanisms influencing thin reservoir resistivity. candidates.title: Application of seismic refraction methods for rock mass characterization at the lead mine tailings site in Olovo Mine

candidates._abstract: In this study, the application of seismic refraction for the characterization of the rock mass at the lead mine tailings facility in Olovo is presented, with the aim of identifying lithostratigraphic horizons, structural discontinuities, and zones of reduced mechanical resistance that may affect tailings stability. The results confirm that seismic refraction, combined with the Delta-t-V method, represents an efficient, non-destructive, and engineering-relevant tool for characterizing complex tailings rock masses. candidates.title: Dating Late Pleistocene pluvial lake shorelines in the Great Basin, USA using rock surface luminescence dating techniques: developing new approaches for challenging lithologies

candidates._abstract: Abstract. This study examines the feasibility of dating pluvial lake beach ridges using rock surface luminescence dating techniques. Directly dating when these gravel clasts were last exposed to sunlight via luminescence is ideal but their limestone and volcanic lithologies prove challenging. Initial measurements from these lithologies show promise. Polymineral extracts from limestone clast surfaces from Coal Valley that contain sufficient detrital sediment exhibited infrared (IR) signals with low to moderate fading rates and properties suited to single-aliquot regenerative (SAR) dose measurement protocols. Surprisingly, there is congruency between luminescence-depth profile plateau ages calculated from inside the volcanic rocks and independent age control. This suggests that some volcanic rocks were small enough to have been bleached throughout their entire thickness in the Late Pleistocene pluvial lake beach environment and that PIRIR signals that record the time of beach ridge formation may be preserved within the rock sub-surface. candidates.title: Impact of Coal Mining on Groundwater Quality and Human Health: A Case Study

candidates._abstract: Groundwater resources in coal mining regions are increasingly threatened by intensive mining activities that alter natural hydrogeochemical conditions and facilitate the mobilization of heavy metals into aquifer systems. The outcomes provide valuable information for environmental managers, policymakers, and mining authorities to support evidence-based groundwater management and safeguard public health in coal mining areas.

candidates.title: Assessment of Active Caps for Metal Remediation in Boreal Shield Lakes Under Varying Temperatures

candidates._abstract: etal and metalloid contamination is a global ecological issue, one that is at risk of accelerating in Canada due to government policies that aim to fast-track mining and associated processing. Two temperature regimes (21⁰C and 4⁰C) were implemented during the column experiment to assess the impact of temperature on metal release from the sediment and on active cap efficiency. Once each column experiment ended, all active caps underwent a Synthetic Precipitation Leaching Experiment (SPLP) to assess if temperature impacted the stability of metal(loid) retention within each cap. Overall, the results indicate that no single amendment can effectively stabilize all target metals in contaminated sediments, particularly under variable temperature conditions. This highlights the need for mixed or multilayered active capping strategies tailored to metal-specific interactions. candidates.title: New geochronological constraints on Late Pleistocene glaciation in the southern Cadí Massif, SE Pyrenees
candidates.authors: Oliva, Marc; Ventura, J.; Çi̇ner, Attila; Sarıkaya, Mehmet Akif; Bonsoms, Josep; Wilcken, Klaus M.

candidates._abstract: ABSTRACT The Cadí Massif (42°17′09″ N, 1°38′11″ E; 2649 m a.s.l.) in the southeastern Pyrenees preserves clear evidence of Late Pleistocene glaciation, although previous research has focused almost exclusively on its northern slope. Paleoclimate simulations indicate that temperatures were ca . 3°C lower during that phase, while precipitation was comparable to present‐day conditions. candidates.title: A global metagenomic atlas uncovers ubiquitous biosynthetic potential linked to adaptation in extreme environments
candidates.authors: Du, Ruibing; He, Ruolin; Qian, Qi; Li, Zhen; Tang, Qi‐Yong; Zhang, Zhidong …

candidates._abstract: Abstract Extreme environments impose severe physicochemical stresses that drive microorganisms to evolve specialized survival strategies. With this catalogue, we identified 162,855 BGCs distributed across 81.5% of MAGs. Gene cluster family analysis showed the strong habitat dependence largely explained by species-level habitat specificity. Metatranscriptomic analyses supported in situ activity of these pathways. In conclusion, we presented a global atlas of biosynthetic potential across extreme-environment microbiota and revealed habitat-dependent patterns of secondary metabolism linked to microbial survival.

candidates.title: Hydrological Dimension of Ladakh under Changing Climate
candidates.authors: Garg, Purushottam Kumar; Singh, Shekhar; Prajapati, Mohit; Farooq, Aamir Jan; Ilyas, Mohd; Karmakar, Ajoy …

candidates._abstract: Ladakh, in the Trans-Himalayan region of northern India, hosts a distinctive high-altitude cold-arid hydrological system in which seasonal snow, glaciers, perched aquifers and a limited network of perennial rivers jointly determine water availability for ecological and human systems. This narrative review-synthesis combines literature analysis (80+ studies) with original trend assessment of IMD gridded rainfall/temperature data (1975–2024) using Modified Mann-Kendall tests and Sen’s slope estimation to comprehend the changes in climate and hydrological dimensions. The synthesis reveals significant warming (+0.02°C yr-1, p<0.05) across Ladakh with spatially variable precipitation trends, earlier snowmelt timing (∼1.2 days yr −1), and glacier mass loss (−0.21 to −0.37 m w.e. yr-¹). Springs show declining perennial discharge while Indus tributaries maintain 62–72% cryospheric runoff contribution. Springs and shallow groundwater systems provide disproportionately important perennial supply where surface waters are strongly seasonal, and precipitation is sparse, and major rivers (notably the upper Indus and tributaries such as the Suru, Zanskar, Shyok, and Nubra) integrate cryospheric and groundwater signals at basin scales. Observational and modelling evidence indicate a system in warming drives earlier snowmelt and a transient increase in glacier runoff, followed by long-term declines in glacier melt contributions as ice volume diminishes; concomitant shifts in recharge reduce spring resilience and alter river seasonality. These dynamics increase exposure to both chronic water scarcity and abrupt hazards. To manage these interconnected risks, we recommend priorities: establishment of integrated high-altitude monitoring networks for snow, ice, springs, and river discharge; process-based modelling that couples downscaled climate projections with cryosphere–groundwater–river interactions; systematic mapping and protection of spring recharge zones; and risk-informed, multi-scale water planning that combines conjunctive use, decentralized storage, and community-based adaptation in the fragile Trans-Himalayan landscapes.

candidates.title: INTERACTIVE EFFECTS OF CLIMATE VARIABILITY ON HEAVY METAL SPECIATION, BIOAVAILABILITY, AND TROPHIC TRANSFER IN FRESHWATER ECOSYSTEMS

candidates._abstract: The convergence of climate variability and legacy heavy metal contamination is reshaping the behavior of potentially toxic elements in freshwater ecosystems worldwide. This review synthesizes current scientific understanding of how changing temperature regimes, hydrological extremes, and biogeochemical alterations influence metal speciation, bioavailability, and trophic transfer across multiple ecological scales. At the global scale, climate-driven hydrological variability and permafrost thaw enhance the mobilization of trace metals from terrestrial reservoirs, while at the environmental scale, shifts in pH, dissolved organic matter, and redox conditions modify chemical speciation and toxicity. At the organismal level, physiological stress and climate-induced toxicant sensitivity amplify metal uptake, disrupt metabolic pathways, and increase susceptibility to bioaccumulation and biomagnification through food webs. Emerging evidence indicates that traditional equilibrium-based models such as the biotic ligand model may underestimate exposure risks under rapidly fluctuating environmental conditions associated with climate change. Furthermore, processes such as mercury methylation, brownification, and acid rock drainage amplify ecosystem-level risks and alter contaminant pathways across freshwater and boreal systems. Integrating multi-scale observational studies with advanced modeling approaches, including kinetic and GIS-based frameworks, is essential for improving prediction and management of metal contamination in a changing climate. Overall, the interaction between climate variability and heavy metal dynamics represents a critical challenge for freshwater ecosystem resilience and requires adaptive, bioavailability-based regulatory frameworks.

candidates.title: Silicate Weathering Dynamics in the Kasaï Basin and Implications for Enhanced Rock Weathering Applications in the Tropics

candidates._abstract: Silicate weathering is one of the ultimate geologic sinks of atmospheric CO2. candidates._abstract: Abstract The Smoking Hills (Ingniryuat) is a polar desert of Arctic Canada that contains naturally occurring streams and ponds of hyperacidic (pH <−2) metal-rich brines (total dissolved solids up to 394,000 mg/L). candidates.title: River carbon delivery from the Hudson Bay Lowlands into Southern Hudson Bay and James Bay

candidates._abstract: Rivers play an important role in the transport of carbon (C) into the global ocean, and en route much C is lost to the atmosphere, buried, or transformed largely by biological or photochemical processes. The fate of river C has implications on greenhouse gas budgets, and downstream ecosystem processes. Many Arctic and subarctic watersheds drain seasonally, or permanently frozen soils, rich in organic C. In particular, the rivers of southwestern Hudson Bay and James Bay (SHBJB) drain the Hudson Bay Lowlands (HBL), which are the world’s second largest contiguous wetland and are estimated to hold in excess of 30 (±6) Pg C. The amount of terrestrial C delivered from the HBL into the adjacent coastal ocean, its seasonality and composition (i.e., organic/inorganic) has yet to be quantified. This knowledge gap has prevented a comprehensive understanding of food web dynamics, nutrient cycling and greenhouse gas budgets in estuarine and marine environments of SHBJB. Since 2023, and through community partnerships, the river C load has been monitored in the lower reaches of the Moose River watershed, and thereafter C monitoring has been expanded to include other major rivers draining the HBL. The dissolved C concentration in the Moose River showed clear seasonality for both dissolved organic carbon (DOC) and dissolved inorganic carbon (DIC), highlighting the importance of seasonal sampling for understanding C dynamics in a region predominantly sampled during the summer. Clear variability was also observed between years as well, suggesting that discharge and precipitation events within a season across years play a key role in C dynamics and delivery. Despite some presence of sporadic discontinuous permafrost in the region, peat derived labile C was minimally found by biodegradability incubations as verified by isotopic ẟ13C-DOC analysis. Empirical relationships were extracted from the Moose River and used to scale for regional estimates, with DOC concentrations being found to increase with increasing: mixed forest cover, watershed area without permafrost, size of watershed, total organic C content in the soil, and broadleaf forest cover. This contemporary C estimate is derived from a dissolved organic load of 3.12 Tg C (2.49 – 3.65 Tg C) and a dissolved inorganic load of 2.31 Tg C (1.96 – 3.26 Tg C). Combining model outputs from this study with published results from eastern James Bay suggests that annually the DOC load for all major rivers draining into James Bay is 3.43 Tg C (2.88 – 3.82 Tg C).

candidates.title: Unveiling Arctic Organic Carbon Cycling Through Amino Acid Radiocarbon Activity: Implications for Paleoclimatic Reconstruction

candidates._abstract: Abstract Constraining the provenance and ultimate fate of sedimentary organic carbon (OC) in the Arctic remains a fundamental challenge, primarily due to the lack of dependable chronological tools. Collectively, these findings demonstrate that THAAs 14 C dating offers a robust pathway for building reliable sediment chronologies in the Arctic, and they underscore that the intrinsic reactivity of different compound classes fundamentally controls how OC is cycled and ultimately buried across major climatic transitions.

candidates.title: Mercury mobilization and export from the Greenland Ice Sheet using an ice-to-ocean approach

candidates.title: From Source Waters to Rivers: Fe‐Rich Colloids Control Carbon and Metal Partitioning in Western Siberian Hydrological Continua
candidates.authors: Krickov, Ivan V.; Loiko, Sergey V.; Lim, Artem G.; Kuzmina, Daria Mikhailovna; Istigechev, Georgy I.; Shirokova, Liudmila S. …

candidates._abstract: ABSTRACT Colloids are a major, but still insufficiently resolved, transport phase linking terrestrial carbon mobilization to riverine export of metals and nutrients. Identifying where colloids form, how they transform along hydrological continua, and which solutes they preferentially carry is essential for predicting biogeochemical responses to permafrost thaw and changing groundwater connectivity. Here we investigated colloidal partitioning of dissolved organic carbon (DOC), major elements and trace metals along four hydrological continua of the Western Siberian Lowland spanning a 1500 km latitudinal transect and a broad climate and permafrost gradient. During summer baseflow, 29 surface waters and soil solutions were size‐fractionated into low‐molecular‐weight (LMW; < 3 kDa) and colloidal (3 kDa–0.45 μm) pools. Two robust patterns emerged. Major ions and Si remained largely in the < 3 kDa fraction, whereas Fe, P and low‐mobility hydrolyzing elements, including Al, Ti, Zr, Hf, Th, U, Pb and the REEs, were predominantly colloidal, especially in streams and rivers. The strongest reorganization of size partitioning occurred not among rivers of different size, but at the transition from source compartments (soil and fen waters) to the first flowing waters. Along the continua, DOC became progressively enriched in the LMW (< 3 kDa) pool, whereas Fe and many trace metals became increasingly colloidal, indicating partial decoupling between carbon and metal transport. Watershed area exerted only a weak, element‐specific influence. In contrast, pH and colloid composition were first‐order controls: increasing pH enhanced the colloidal fractions of Fe, P, Y, Zr, Th, U and REEs, but increased the low‐molecular‐weight fractions of alkali and alkaline‐earth elements and Mo. Ratio‐based, correlational and PCA analyses consistently identified Fe/Al‐rich organo‐mineral colloids as the dominant carriers of low‐solubility elements, with REEs and P showing stronger affinity for Fe‐rich than for Al‐rich colloids. Similar carrier‐based partitioning reported from humid tropical humic systems suggests that Fe/Al‐rich colloidal transport is not restricted to permafrost landscapes, but may represent a broader mechanism in organic‐rich hydrological systems. In Western Siberia, the permafrost gradient provides a space‐for‐time framework in which future changes in colloidal partitioning are expected to reflect active‐layer deepening and increasing surface–subsurface water exchange.

candidates.title: Application of Passive and Active Remediation Methods in the Treatment of Areas Contaminated by Acid Mine Drainage
candidates.authors: Wittenberger, Gabriel
candidates.found_via: query “natural acid rock drainage” ; query “acid rock drainage vegetation”
candidates._abstract: Remediation of areas affected by acid mine drainage (AMD) remains a persistent environmental and technical challenge, particularly in regions with a long history of mining. AMD is characterized by low pH and elevated concentrations of dissolved metals and sulfates, leading to long-term degradation of soil and water environments. This paper evaluates selected remediation approaches applied under the geological and hydrogeological conditions of the Slovak Republic. The study is based on laboratory experiments, field investigations, and pilot-scale systems implemented at sites with different types of contamination. Special attention is given to passive treatment systems, including anoxic limestone drains, anaerobic bioreactors, and constructed wetlands, as well as selected active remediation techniques. The results confirmed high metal removal efficiency in passive systems, with some cases exceeding 95%, particularly for iron and selected trace elements. In contrast, sulfate reduction proved to be the main limiting factor, strongly influenced by hydraulic retention time, substrate composition, and operational stability. The findings highlight both the potential and limitations of passive and active approaches and emphasize the importance of appropriate system design and optimized hydraulic conditions for long-term remediation effectiveness.

candidates.title: Integrating metal removal efficiency and bioclimatic adaptation in the selection of macrophytes for acid mine drainage treatment
candidates.authors: Cárdenas-Gaudry, Marí; Pumaylle, Johana; Unocc, Ronald
candidates.found_via: query “natural acid rock drainage” ; query “acid rock drainage vegetation”
candidates._abstract: Acid mine drainage (AMD) is one of the main environmental liabilities associated with mining activity due to its high acidity and elevated concentrations of metals and metalloids. In this context, phytoremediation using macrophytes represents a sustainable alternative for the passive treatment of these effluents. This review article comparatively evaluated eighteen macrophyte species considering their metal removal efficiency, pH tolerance, and bioclimatic adaptation. The results identified Vetiveria zizanioides as the species with the highest tolerance to acidic conditions, supporting pH values as low as 2.7 and increasing the effluent toward near-neutral conditions. In contrast, Juncus effusus, Typha orientalis, and Phragmites australis achieved removal efficiencies close to 99% for Fe, Mn, and As, as well as efficiencies above 90% for Zn, Cd, and Al. Copper removal showed the lowest efficiencies due to its high mobility and ionic competition under acidic conditions. Furthermore, the bioclimatic analysis revealed that variables such as biotemperature, precipitation, and water availability directly influence the stability and performance of macrophytes in treatment systems. It is concluded that the selection of macrophytes for AMD treatment should integrate geochemical, physiological, and bioclimatic criteria in order to optimize the efficiency and sustainability of constructed wetlands.

candidates.title: Assessment of Treatment Technologies and Research on Governance Models for Acid Mine Drainage from Closed Coal Mines in Karst Regions
candidates.authors: Li, Chong; Jiao, Yanan; Zhao, Xiaoying; Yang, Bin; 白波
candidates.found_via: query “natural acid rock drainage” ; query “acid rock drainage vegetation”
candidates._abstract: Acid mine drainage (AMD) pollution from closed coal mines in karst regions represents a major environmental challenge in the global mining industry. The complexity of hydrogeological conditions in such regions leads to significant challenges in both predictability and controllability of pollution. Taking the Yudong River Basin in Guizhou Province, Southwest China, as the study area, and based on six years (2017–2023) of systematic remediation practices and monitoring data, this study systematically evaluates the effectiveness and applicable conditions of three types of treatment technologies: centralized treatment stations, source control combined with end-of-pipe treatment, and water-sealing ecological plugging. On this basis, governance models applicable to karst regions are distilled. The results show that after six years of remediation, the number of pollution points in the Yudong River Basin decreased from 27 to 12. At the outflow section, the total Fe reduction rate reached 88.3%, the total Mn reduction rate reached 62.3%, and the proportion of contaminated river length was reduced by 78.5%. Each of the three technologies has its own applicable conditions. Centralized treatment stations, characterized by mature technology but high operational costs, are suitable for emergency transition periods. Source control combined with end-of-pipe treatment addresses both symptoms and root causes, making it applicable to complex pollution points. Water-sealing ecological plugging, although cost-controllable, carries a risk of secondary pollution in karst-developed areas. The failure of water-sealing ecological plugging technology is mainly attributed to two mechanisms: bypass flow through karst conduits and overflow induced by water level rise. Based on the six-year remediation practice, this study proposes a source control model for karst conduits centered on the core concepts of “filling, isolating, plugging, intercepting, draining, and controlling”. The implementation process consists of four stages: detailed investigation, graded optimization, stepwise implementation, and long-term monitoring. The core innovation lies in the cross-disciplinary application of coal mine water control techniques to environmental remediation, achieving a shift from passive end-of-pipe treatment to active source control. This model can provide theoretical reference and practical guidance for karst mining areas in Southwest China and other regions with similar geological conditions.

candidates.title: Relação relevo-rocha-solo na Península Ulu, Ilha James Ross, Antártica
candidates.authors: Villela, Fernando Nadal Junqueira; Palma, Heitor Paiva; Cazaroto, Pamela Cristina; Tavares, Beatriz Marina; Dariolli, Larissa Scavassa; Nývlt, Daniel …
candidates.found_via: query “acid drainage proglacial” ; query “Pyrenees acid rock drainage”
candidates._abstract: Na Península Ulu (PU), Ilha James Ross (IJR), localizada no Mar de Weddell, lado oriental da Península Antártica, é possível observar uma relação única de relevo-rocha-solo devido à configuração da paisagem, exemplificada por relevos em mesa e superfícies sedimentares erosivas como principais compartimentos geomorfológicos. Para melhor compreender essas relações, este trabalho visa fornecer uma análise integrada das características do relevo, rocha e solo por meio de três transectos do topo ao fundo de vale, explorando desde a topografia, litologia, cobertura pedológica e diferenciações ambientais, até os processos e feições peri, para e progaciais. Desta forma, três unidades de paisagem puderam ser identificadas na Península em questão: Planaltos Basálticos, Escarpas e a Superfície de Erosão. Os Planaltos Basálticos (310 – 380 m a.n.m.) correspondem aos relevos tabulares formados por fluxos hialoclásticos e basálticos de idade Neogênica, associados a deltas alimentados por fluxos de lava misturados com depósitos subaquáticos, que atualmente configuram as formas de relevo em mesa ou cone de escória da PU; predominam os processos periglaciais, como por exemplo, o congelamento/degelo, crioturbação, rastejo e segregação de partículas, aplainando as formas de relevo por crioplanação e nivação, com a formação de solos com padrões classificados como Criossolos com características Esqueléticas e Áridas. As Escarpas (200 – 310 m a.n.m.) são sustentadas por coberturas deltaicas e camadas frontais do Grupo Vulcânico da Ilha James Ross, do Neógeno, e configuram penhascos cujas vertentes são dominadas por processos paraglaciais como, por exemplo, movimentos gravitacionais de massa e solifluxão, apresentando encostas recobertas por cascalho, lóbulos de solifluxão e depósitos de tálus; na base das escarpas, lagos proglaciais são alimentados por morainas com núcleos de gelo, campos de neve e geleiras, e rochas e sedimentos dispostos nas encostas geram Criossolos descontinuamente, com características coluviais. Finalmente, a Superfície de Erosão (abaixo de 200 m a.n.m.) é sustentada por sedimentos marinhos cretáceos compostos principalmente por leitos de argilito e arenito de diversas formações geológicas, formando um glacis de interflúvios suaves a ondulados com gradientes de declive variados e quebras/mudanças de declive convexas e côncavas, que alternam com vales em forma de U e V; nesta unidade predominam processos paraglaciais, ou seja, movimentos gravitacionais de massa e solifluxão, com a formação de planícies fluviais de rios entrelaçados e Criossolos com características Arênicas e Coluviais. Além disso, a camada ativa e o permafrost estão espalhados por toda a UP, mas por vezes podem ser descontínuos, principalmente na unidade de paisagem da superfície de erosão. O trabalho mostrou que as informações geológicas, geomorfológicas e pedológicas da IJR e da PU podem ser compreendidas pelos princípios adotados na abordagem metodológica, que envolvem a Teoria Geral de Sistemas e a Geoecologia da Paisagem, incluindo a produção de perfis bidimensionais e a compartimentação do relevo.

candidates.title: Microbial community succession and biogeochemical activity in deglaciating polar ecosystems
candidates.authors: Sugden, Scott
candidates.found_via: query “acid drainage proglacial” ; query “proglacial soil acidification pyrite”
candidates._abstract: Almost 10% of Earth’s land area is covered by glacial ice, but as glaciers continue to melt due to ongoing climate change, more than 150,000 km2 of glaciated area will be exposed by 2100. The nutrient-poor, newly deglaciated soils exposed by glacial retreat are quickly colonized by microbial communities that establish soil nutrient pools, promote soil development, and support future plant colonization. Because soils drive terrestrial cycles of carbon, nitrogen, and other nutrients, an understanding of microbial succession and activity in rapidly expanding postglacial ecosystems will be crucial for predicting future biogeochemical dynamics in polar regions. In this thesis, I therefore used a comprehensive suite of molecular techniques to better understand the patterns, drivers, and biogeochemical consequences of microbial succession in deglaciating polar ecosystems. First, I performed a metabarcoding survey of both bacteria and microeukaryotes to characterize how community structure and composition vary with exposure age and test for shared drivers of succession across forefields, domains, abundance fractions, and soil depths. For this analysis, I collected both surface (0-3 cm) and deep (15 cm) soil samples along chronosequences that I established in five glacier forefields in the Canadian High Arctic and Antarctic Peninsula, encompassing soils deglaciated for 5 to 200 years. Despite substantial geographic variation in species pools, succession in all forefields was characterized by increasing cell populations and OTU richness, decelerating rates of community turnover, increasing spatial heterogeneity, and the accumulation of low-abundance, phylogenetically clustered taxa. These shared successional patterns were often modulated by local variation among microbial domains, abundance classes, and soil depths.Because chronosequence-based studies implicitly assume that time is the primary driver of observed community differences, I then tested this assumption using a reciprocal soil transplantation experiment. Recently exposed soils were moved up to 400 m further from a glacier front, and older soils were relocated back to the periglacial environment. Microbial community responses, measured one year after transplantation, were strongly directional: colonization and succession proceeded rapidly in young, nutrient-poor soils released from the constraints of low periglacial temperatures and high soil moisture, whereas communities in older, more nutrient-rich soils resisted retrogression when these constraints were reimposed. These results suggest that postglacial successional trajectories are driven not solely by time but also by distance from the glacier, with time playing an increasingly stronger role in older communities. Finally, I assessed the biogeochemical activities characteristic of different soil ages, with an emphasis on carbon and nitrogen accumulation and turnover. Metagenomic and metatranscriptomic sequencing from one Arctic and one Antarctic chronosequence revealed a shift from litho- to photoautotrophic metabolisms over time, decreasing metabolic flexibility in electron donors and acceptors, increasing heterotrophic substrate diversity, and a growing soil methane sink. These results were complemented with in situ gas flux measurements and an ex situ isotope-tracing experiment using 13CO2 and 15N2. Fluorescence in situ hybridization and nanoscale secondary ion mass spectroscopy confirmed the metabolic shift from litho- to photoautotrophic metabolisms and revealed that most carbon and nitrogen fixation activity was restricted to a small proportion of highly active cells. Overall, my results demonstrate the pathways and processes that drive soil development and biogeochemical activity in one of the most rapidly changing ecosystems on the planet and serve as foundational information for predictive efforts to understand the future polar landscape.

candidates.title: Quetico: An Identity–Persistence Field Companion
candidates.authors: Bostick, Devin
candidates.found_via: query “sulfide oxidation glacier retreat water quality” ; query “rock glacier spring nickel sulfate”
candidates._abstract: Abstract Quetico: An Identity–Persistence Field Companion applies the structural vocabulary of the Identity–Persistence Program to the natural history of Quetico Provincial Park and the surrounding boreal landscape. It is neither an ecology textbook nor a proof extension. Its purpose is to show how a declared structural lens can organize observation across geological, hydrological, ecological, biological, and institutional scales without replacing the domain-specific sciences that supply the facts. The companion follows persistence through glacial formation, soils, lakes, forests, wetlands, carbon cycling, succession, disturbance, food webs, wildlife, fire, climate pressure, governance, and conservation. Throughout, structural interpretations are kept distinct from empirical claims, modeled estimates, contested findings, and open scientific questions. The framework contributes no ecological facts of its own; it supplies a grammar for asking what persists, what transforms, what bounds remain operative, and when a change should instead be read as rupture, branching, or regime change. The result is both a worked application and a field guide: a way to carry formal attention into a real landscape while preserving uncertainty, narrative, and surprise. The lens structures the inquiry but does not exhaust the place.

candidates.title: Systematic Review of Metallic, Industrial, and Pharmaceutical Emerging Contaminants in Snow and Ice: A Global Perspective from Polar and High-Mountain Regions
candidates.authors: Spagnesi, Azzurra; Gambaro, Andrea; Barbaro, Elena; Gabrieli, Jacopo; Barbante, Carlo
candidates.found_via: query “permafrost thaw stream acidification metals” ; query “proglacial soil acidification pyrite”
candidates._abstract: Emerging contaminants (ECs) comprise diverse pollutant classes that are increasingly detected in remote environments due to their persistence and long-range transport potential. In cold regions, atmospheric cold-trapping processes favour their accumulation in high-altitude and high-latitude snow and ice, which act as sensitive archives and secondary sources of contamination. While previous studies have addressed individual environmental compartments (e.g., snowpack, glacier ice, meltwater), focusing on specific contaminant classes, a systematic review integrating the occurrence, behaviour and impacts of major EC groups in polar and alpine snow and ice is still lacking. To fill this gap, this work synthesised current knowledge on the environmental fate of three key EC categories in the cryosphere: metals and metalloids (MMs), industrial chemicals and by-products (ICBs), and pharmaceuticals and personal care products (PPCPs). PRISMA guidelines were accurately followed for research, which was based on a Google Scholar search combining keywords on cryospheric matrices (snow, firn, ice cores), geographical regions (Arctic, Antarctic, Alps, high mountains), and contaminant classes. Of 350 records initially identified, 300 met the eligibility criteria (post-industrial snow, firn, or ice cores studies) after excluding studies focused on aerosol or meltwater-only, method-focused papers, pre-industrial datasets, urban-only investigations, and duplicates. Risk of bias was qualitatively assessed through manual screening, evaluating matrix eligibility, temporal consistency, analytical methods, detection limits, and duplicate data, with particular attention to inconsistencies in ECs classification. Strict operational definitions were therefore applied to ensure methodological coherence. Concentration data were harmonised into a standardised database, and findings were synthesised through a structured narrative supported by tabulated datasets organised by matrix and site. Overall, the evidence indicates widespread occurrence of ECs in the global cryosphere, with spatial variability linked to emission sources, long-range transport pathways, and snow physicochemical properties. Climate-change-driven alterations of snow dynamics, glacier retreat and permafrost thaw are expected to modify partitioning equilibria and enhance the secondary release of legacy and contemporary contaminants. However, significant limitations persist, including geographical gaps, variability in analytical sensitivity, lack of long-term monitoring for certain EC classes, and inconsistencies in contaminant classification frameworks. Despite these constraints, the synthesis highlights consistent emerging patterns and underscores the need to strengthen existing environmental protocols to mitigate potential risks to ecosystems and human health.

candidates.title: Hydrogeochemical controls on arsenic, boron, lithium, and antimony in volcanic–geothermal systems: Evidence from the Central Bolivian Altiplano
candidates.authors: Tapia, María Isabel Chambi; Lima, Israel Quino; Ormachea, Mauricio; Quispe, Delia Jallurana; Paco, Nancy Chavez; Šráček, Ondra …
candidates.found_via: query “Cordillera Blanca water quality metals” ; query “Cordillera Blanca acid”
candidates._abstract: Volcanic-geothermal systems exert strong hydrogeochemical controls on the mobility and accumulation of geogenic trace elements (TEs) in groundwater, surface water, and sediments. This study investigates the processes governing the mobilization and enrichment of arsenic (As), boron (B), lithium (Li), and antimony (Sb) in water and sediments of volcanic–geothermal environments in the central part of the Bolivian Cordillera Occidental from the Altiplano. It is characterized by Oligoce-Holocene age dacitic–andesitic volcanic rocks, ignimbrites, pyroclastic deposits, lacustrine fluvial sediment and active geothermal manifestations. Two field campaigns conducted during the rainy season (RS) and dry season (DS) evaluated spatial and seasonal variability through hydrochemical characterization, geochemical calculations, statistical analyses, and sediment contamination indices. The GW and SW hydrochemical facies are dominated by Na–Ca–HCO 3 , Na–Ca–Mg–HCO 3 , and Na–Cl–HCO 3 facies, with a relative dominance of Na + during the DS. The concentrations of As, B, Li, and Sb exceeded the Bolivian (NB-512), WHO and U.S. Health-based Screening Levels (HBSLs) guidelines, reached maximum values to 1793 μg/L for As and 28156 μg/L for B, particularly in hot springs of the Caripe and Sajama regions. The enrichment of these TEs appears to be associated with weathering of volcanic materials, interaction with hydrothermally altered deposits and geothermal precipitates, evaporation-driven solute concentration and retention-remobilization processes within sediments. The hydrogeochemical modeling suggests that Fe-oxides/hydroxides, carbonate precipitation, and silicate weathering influence TEs mobility and retention. The sediment contamination indices indicate moderate to extreme enrichment of As and B supporting predominantly geogenic origin. These findings improve the understanding of TEs behavior in volcanic–geothermal systems and provides a practical scientific basis for source-specific monitoring, risk management and mitigation strategies in regions where groundwater and surface water are directly used for drinking, livestock, and irrigation.

candidates.title: Differences in potassium and chlorine incorporation in members of an alpine stream food web in the West Carpathians
candidates.authors: Janiga, Martin; Janiga, Marián; Tuchyňa, Jakub; Pánik, Patrik; Ballová, Zuzana Kompišová
candidates.found_via: query “Cordillera Blanca water quality metals” ; query “Cordillera Blanca acid”
candidates._abstract: Introduction High mountain streams are experiencing pronounced shifts in precipitation regimes and water chemistry; however, it remains unclear how organisms inhabiting these systems influence the transfer of chemical elements through food webs. Methods We measured concentrations of potassium and chlorine in algae, grazing mayflies, predatory stoneflies, and Alpine Bullhead ( Cottus poecilopus ) across seasons in an alpine stream. Results Algae exhibited marked seasonal variation, with higher potassium accumulation during the main summer growth period despite relatively stable water concentrations. Grazing mayflies maintained stable potassium levels but showed increased chlorine during colder months when chlorine concentrations in water were elevated. Predatory stoneflies showed only minor seasonal variation, with a slight increase in potassium in winter. The Alpine Bullhead did not exhibit significant seasonal changes in potassium or chlorine accumulation in its skull. Following major flood events, potassium and chlorine concentrations tended to co-vary across trophic levels, whereas under baseflow conditions they often varied independently. Discussion These patterns suggest that different trophic groups regulate element accumulation according to their physiology, life history, and ecological roles. The decoupling of organismal and water chemistry indicates that environmental concentrations alone do not fully explain element distribution within alpine stream food webs. Our findings provide new insights into element dynamics and highlight the importance of biological mediation in high-mountain ecosystems under changing environmental conditions.

candidates.title: Venas hidrotermales de barita en rocas metapelíticas del suroccidente del Macizo de Santander, Colombia: evidencias de ebullición y fluidos moderadamente salinos ricos en sulfato
candidates.authors: Quintero, Fabián Camilo Bonilla; Mantilla-Figueroa, Luis Carlos; Sánchez, Leonardo Palmera; Hernández, Rafael Cabanzo
candidates.found_via: query “Cordillera Blanca water quality metals” ; query “Cordillera Blanca acid”
candidates._abstract: Este estudio analiza venas hidrotermales de barita en rocas metapelíticas pre-Devónicas de la Unidad de Esquistos de Chicamocha, en el sector suroccidental del Macizo de Santander. La barita ocurre como cristales bladed blancos a rosados, asociados con calcita, óxidos y cuarzo, rellenando fracturas tardías con rumbo WNW–ESE. Análisis cualitativos de DRX confirmaron barita y calcita como las principales fases minerales. La petrografía de inclusiones fluidas revela la coexistencia (FIAs), de inclusiones bifásicas ricas en líquido e inclusiones monofásicas de vapor, con relaciones líquido/vapor variables. Estas características indican atrapamiento heterogéneo, consistente con un proceso de ebullición. La microtermometría muestra temperaturas de primera fusión del hielo cercanas a -40 °C, compatibles con un sistema H₂O-NaCl-CaCl2, y temperaturas de fusión final del hielo entre -6,1 y -14,0 °C, correspondientes a salinidades de 9,3-17,8 % masa eq. NaCl. Las temperaturas de homogenización presentan una amplia dispersión y valores aparentes elevados (>300 °C), reflejando los efectos del atrapamiento heterogéneo. La espectroscopía Raman aplicada a inclusiones fluidas primarias muestra una banda intensa a 980-983 cm⁻¹ atribuida al ion sulfato en la barita, junto con picos característicos del grupo SO42- en solución. La deconvolución de la banda de estiramiento O-H permitió estimar salinidades relativas entre 13,6 y 21,6 % masa eq. NaCl coherentes con los datos microtermométricos. En conjunto, los resultados indican que las venas precipitaron a partir de fluidos hidrotermales acuosos, moderadamente salinos y ricos en sulfato. La ausencia de fuentes locales de azufre sugiere que el fluido se originó en las formaciones Rosablanca y Paja, movilizado por fluidos de cuenca que infiltraron el basamento metamórfico. Este trabajo documenta una ocurrencia previamente no reportada de barita hidrotermal en el Macizo de Santander, aportando nuevos elementos para comprender la circulación de fluidos y los eventos hidrotermales tardíos en el norte de los Andes colombianos.

candidates.title: Population‐Specific Chemotypes in Pseudomisopates rivas‐martinezii (Sanchez Mata) Güemes From La Serrota and Gredos Massifs (Iberian Central Range)
candidates.authors: Sánchez‐Hernández, Eva; Amat, María Elena; Cano‐Pérez, Mario; García, Vicente González; Martín‐Gil, Jesús; Martín‐Ramos, Pablo
candidates.found_via: query “Cordillera Blanca water quality metals” ; query “Cordillera Blanca acid”
candidates._abstract: Pseudomisopates rivas-martinezii (Sánchez Mata) Güemes (Plantaginaceae) is a critically endangered endemic species from the Iberian Central Range. This study characterizes population-specific chemotypes in aerial and underground tissues from La Serrota and Gredos populations using elemental analysis, Fourier-transform infrared (FTIR) spectroscopy, and gas chromatography-mass spectrometry (GC-MS). Elemental analysis revealed interpopulation differences in aerial nitrogen content (1.0% vs. 1.9%). FTIR showed interpopulation and tissue-specific variations. GC-MS characterization revealed convergent composition of underground parts dominated by histidine-derived metabolites, but significant divergence in aerial profiles reflecting differential aromatic amino acid metabolism from the shikimic acid pathway. La Serrota aerial tissues were characterized by phenolic derivatives (phenylalanine/tyrosine products), while Gredos specimens exhibited predominance of nitrogenous heterocyclic compounds (tryptophan catabolism products). These findings suggest differential selective pressures acting on organs and populations, with implications for conservation strategies and taxonomic understanding of this monospecific genus.

candidates.title: 40-kyr of environmental history of the southeastern sector of paleolake Cuitzeo, central-western Mexico: Insights from abiotic and biotic proxies
candidates.authors: Pérez-Rodríguez, Nayeli; Morales, Juan; Israde-Alcántara, Isabel; Domínguez-Vázquez, Gabriela; Cervantes-Solano, Miguel Ángel; Goguitchaichvili, Avto …
candidates.found_via: query “Cordillera Blanca water quality metals” ; query “Cordillera Blanca acid”
candidates._abstract: We present a multiproxy reconstruction of environmental changes recorded in the southeastern sector of Lake Cuitzeo (central-western Mexico) over the last ∼40 kyr. Our study integrates abiotic (major-element geochemistry, rock-magnetic parameters, pH, and electrical conductivity) and biotic proxies (diatoms and pollen) from a ∼10 m-long sedimentary core (Cz-07). This multiproxy approach provides a robust framework for identifying variations in terrigenous input, redox conditions, nutrient availability, carbonate precipitation, and hydrological balance, as well as the response of local vegetation to climate fluctuations. Comparing the Cz-07 record with previous data from a depocenter core reveals some spatial differences in the lake’s sensitivity to environmental changes. The sequence indicates generally low lake levels between ∼42 and ∼26.5 kyr BP, followed by pronounced environmental variability during the Last Glacial Maximum, including a marked dry episode at its onset. Enhanced runoff and predominantly oxic conditions characterize the interval from ∼17.5 to ∼11 kyr BP, encompassing the Bølling–Allerød and Younger Dryas events. During the early-to-middle Holocene (∼11.7–5 kyr BP), a progressive shift toward arid conditions is evidenced by increased carbonate precipitation, higher salinity, and reduced runoff. The most severe drought occurred during the middle Holocene, causing a substantial contraction of the lake’s southeastern sector. This arid phase aligns with middle Holocene drying trends reported in other lacustrine records across central Mexico.

candidates.title: Multiproxy Approach for Identification of Sequence Stratigraphic Elements: Implications on Continental Sequence Stratigraphy
candidates.authors: Saha, Abhirup; Gogoi, Ankita; Chetia, Rajashree; Bhuyan, Diganta; Kalita, Pranjit
candidates.found_via: query “Pyrenees acid rock drainage” ; query “Pyrenees ferricrete”
candidates._abstract: The applications of sequence stratigraphy are mostly limited to areas in the vicinity of the shoreline. However, due to lack of distinct geological markers, its application to fine-grained continental and deep-marine sediments remains restricted. Hence a multi-proxy approach that integrates sedimentological, mineralogical, and chemostratigraphic proxies from both marine and continental successions is used with a focus on continental domains. The shifting trends of accommodation to sediment supply are comparable to the shifting trends of several proxies, which indicates the utility of such proxies in constraining the sequence stratigraphic architecture. Clay mineral assemblages indicate weathering and paleoclimatic conditions, while paleosols reflect subaerial exposure and landscape stability. Decreasing Ti/Al, Zr/Al and Si/Al ratios marks shift from continental to marine influence. In case of the lacustrine settings or glacial lakes, periodic paleoredox fluctuations and glacial-cycles can be constrained using Ti/Zr ratios. Upstream, high sediment supply leads to depleted Mo and V, while downstream, anoxic conditions promote organic matter preservation. T/SF trends distinguish upstream from downstream river segments. Similarly varying trends of the T/SF are utilized to interpret the upstream and downstream portions of a river system. However, several limitations are often associated with using these proxies, which have to be accounted for. The present review work documents the utility, applicability and limitations of such proxies using several case studies from marine and transitional settings and proposes their applicability in continental domain. By documenting changes in sediment supply, accommodation space, and water chemistry, this multi-proxy technique enables the reconstruction of transgressive–regressive cycles and systems tracts in fine-grained deposits, as observed in several case studies. The work demonstrates that the combination of all these proxies significantly enhances the reliability of sequence stratigraphic interpretations, despite intrinsic limitations.

candidates.title: Estimación de la calidad del agua superficial mediante el análisis multitemporal de la reflectancia en la Subcuenca del Río Negro
candidates.authors: More, Eyvind Francisco Herrera
candidates.venue: Universidad Peruana Cayetano Heredia Institutional Repository
candidates.found_via: query “drenaje ácido de roca glaciar” ; query “drenaje ácido Cordillera Blanca”
candidates._abstract: El retroceso glaciar está generando una serie de impactos en los Andes peruanos, entre ellos el deterioro de la calidad del agua debido a la ocurrencia del drenaje ácido de roca (DAR). Tradicionalmente, la caracterización de la calidad del agua se basa en muestreos in situ con equipos multiparámetro y análisis en laboratorio; sin embargo, estos métodos presentan limitaciones espaciotemporales que dificultan el análisis y una mejor comprensión de los efectos del DAR a nivel de cuenca y a largo plazo. Este estudio evalúa la variabilidad multitemporal de la reflectancia de cuerpos de agua como indicador de los cambios en la calidad del agua en la subcuenca Río Negro – Cordillera Blanca. A partir de la clasificación de los cuerpos de agua, se identificó que aquellos impactados por DAR presentan valores de reflectancia mayores en comparación con aquellos no impactados (p < 0.001; prueba t de Student y Mann-Whitney U). Con base en ello, se desarrollaron índices físicos para estimar los parámetros pH y conductividad eléctrica mediante combinaciones de bandas de la región visible, empleando imágenes de tres sensores satelitales. Las regresión con Planet PSB.SD obtuvo los errores más bajos en general, seguida de Sentinel-2 MSI y Landsat 8 OLI. Las estimaciones para el periodo 2013–2025 evidenciaron variaciones espaciales y temporales en la calidad del agua asociadas a procesos como el retroceso glaciar, particularmente en la laguna Tararhua, donde se observó una tendencia decreciente del pH (prueba de Mann–Kendall, p < 0.05). En contraste, lagunas ubicadas en zonas sin influencia glaciar, tales como Capac Cocha y Orococha, mantuvieron condiciones relativamente estables (pH > 5.5 y conductividad eléctrica < 150 μS/cm). La aplicación de los modelos propuestos en la laguna B de la subcuenca Llaca confirma su potencial de transferencia a entornos geográficos de condiciones similares. Este estudio apoyará en la comprensión de los procesos espaciotemporales de la ocurrencia de DAR y destaca a la teledetección como una herramienta eficaz complementaria para mejorar el monitoreo de la calidad del agua en cuencas crecientemente afectadas por el cambio climático y otros impactos humanos.

candidates.title: Phytoremediation of Coal Mine Acid Drainage Using the Invasive Weed Cyperus rotundus and Typha angustifolia: Optimizing Biomass Density in a Substrate-Free Batch System
candidates.authors: Rahmadhani, Rinda; Huda, Muhammad Mahfuzh; Adawiyah, Rabiatul; Ivena, Jevon Ona
candidates.found_via: query “acid rock drainage vegetation” ; query “acid rock drainage plant traits”
candidates._abstract: Acid mine drainage (AMD) presents a persistent environmental challenge, particularly in tropical mining regions. This study evaluated the phytoremediation potential of the zero-cost invasive weed Cyperus rotundus against the established hyperaccumulator Typha angustifolia in a substrate-free batch system. Utilizing extreme raw AMD (pH 2.69; Fe 6.40 ppm; TDS 1,390 ppm), the experiment encompassed a baseline comparison (9 clumps), density optimization (6–15 clumps), and a synergistic mixed-culture evaluation over 15 days. Baseline results indicated that T. angustifolia intrinsically outperformed C. rotundus in iron (Fe) removal (89.10% vs. 82.22%) by day 10. However, optimizing C. rotundus to a 15-clump saturation threshold successfully overcame this deficit, achieving 91.20% Fe attenuation (0.56 ppm). Crucially, extended hydraulic retention (15 days) in high-density configurations induced a severe secondary pollution event, catastrophically increasing Total Dissolved Solids (TDS) to 2,300 ppm because of biomass carrying capacity limits and necrosis. The mixed-culture configuration exhibited the highest overall efficacy, maximizing Fe removal (92.63%), buffering pH to 3.27, and moderating late-stage TDS spikes. The findings demonstrated that while C. rotundus was a highly viable bioremediator, engineering designs needed to cap biomass at the saturation threshold and strictly enforce a 6- to 10-day retention window to prevent secondary decay pollution.

candidates.title: Evaluation of drainage and well water for drinking and agricultural use in calcareous soils
candidates.authors: Abdulrazzaq, Mohammed H. M.; Al-Rawi, Ali Abdulhadi; Abdul-Azeez, H M
candidates.found_via: query “acid rock drainage vegetation” ; query “acid rock drainage plant traits”
candidates._abstract: Severe water scarcity and qualitative degradation increasingly threaten rural ecosystems in arid countries like Iraq due to declining transboundary allocations and intensive agricultural pesticide applications. This research evaluated the surface and groundwater quality within wells and streams located in specific rural regions. In countryside areas in Iraq, the pointed problems of low groundwater levels and high usage of pesticides by the farmers lead to low water quality in terms of physical and chemical components especially in wells. The water resources are used in countryside areas for irrigation, animal and domestic demands. The quality of the water was measured according to the Iraqi quality standard specifications for drinking water and irrigation (Iraqi quality standards, 2010), the World Health Organization guidelines (WHO, 2011) and the US Environmental Protection Agency regulations (USEPA) (1975). The collected data are compiled and compared to the specification limits of these standards. The outcomes of the present study show the proportion of water points acceptable for agricultural irrigation, highlighting options for salt-tolerant crops based on localised salinity parameters. While a distinct 10 wells met standard regulatory criteria for drinking water based on pH, salinity and total hardness. While other wells appear to have high ionic concentration and high amount of salt dissolved in water causing them to be excluded from considerations for human use and irrigation and making them viable only for highly salt-tolerant crops. Overall, the results uncovered that salinity and ionic components are the major factors determining water quality and its suitability for irrigation or human uses in rural environments, as well as whether there is a benefit to invest there.

candidates.title: Effect of Soil Physical and Organic Matter on Soil Erodibility in Duhok Dam Sub Drainage Basin
candidates.authors: Abdulrahman, Haliz; Ahmed, Hiveen; Al-Silevany, Baybeen
candidates.venue: Kirkuk University Journal For Agricultural Sciences
candidates.found_via: query “acid rock drainage vegetation” ; query “acid rock drainage plant traits”
candidates._abstract: Soil erosion is a barrier to achieving sustainable land use especially in semi-arid regions with multiple soil types. This work evaluates the soil erodibility factor (K) at twelve sampling locations in Duhok Dam (Kurdistan Region, Iraq). The investigates impact of key physical and chemical soil properties including Bulk density, permeability, organic matter, textural and structural properties of these soil samples. Organic matter content and soil texture were found to be the major drivers for controlling K-factor under different land uses, according the sensitivity analysis. The sensitivity to erosion decreased with increasing clay content of the soils, while sandy soils suffered from greater susceptibility to the erosion because of their lower permeability. The k-values had been predicted by a regression model, which accounted for 98.66% of the total variance (R2 = 98.6%). The increasing of bulk density and permeability have variable effects on erodibility. Study of various soil properties show significant correlations between Bulk density, erodibility (K), permeability and OM content indicating useful information about the behavior and erosiveness property of the soil. The positive relationship between erodibility and bulk density implies that denser soils are more easily eroded, possibly because reduced porosity in such soils results in increased surface runoff. It is also interesting to note that as the erodibility increases, the permeability of soils tends to increase, thus, with greater water movement in susceptible soils, detachment and transport of particles could be quickened. On the other hand, the soil bulk density had a negative relationship with organic matter content, which is evidence of the importance of organic materials for maintaining good soil structure and reducing compaction. This emphasizes the interdependence between soil physical properties and their joint impact on land degradation, and draws attention for integrated soil management strategies aimed at mitigating the risk of erosion in vulnerable catchments.

candidates.title: Melting Microbiomes in Permafrost: Implications for Greenhouse Gas Emissions
candidates._abstract: Permafrost, the perpetually frozen ground that covers roughly a quarter of the Northern Hemisphere, stores approximately twice as much carbon as the atmosphere currently holds.As global warming causes thawing, latent microbial populations revive and decompose old organic materials into CO₂ and CH₄.However, microbiological processes that drive these emissions are inadequately represented in climate models, resulting in significant uncertainty in permafrost-carbon feedback forecasts.This chapter covers recent research on microbial succession, redox changes, and hydrological factors that influence greenhouse gas emissions during thaw.Aerobic oxidation is predominant in well-drained uplands, while anaerobic methanogenesis in waterlogged thermokarst soils and lakes causes CH₄ hotspots.Emerging omics, isotopic, and remote sensing methods are increasingly revealing how microbial metabolisms relate to landscape emissions.Integrating microbial dynamics into Earth-system models is critical for refining forecasts and guiding mitigation actions.Understanding the "melting microbiome" is therefore crucial in limiting the Arctic's impact to global warming.

candidates.title: Melting Permafrost: An emerging climate hazard and environmental disaster risk
candidates.authors: S., Jeevika; S., Nandha Kishore; V., Prabhanjan; Jidhu, Vaishnavi S.
